ideas.arrival: built in the 2020s, about 0 years after it was imagined
ideas.author: Ray Naylor
ideas.line: A computer that opens itself out into working shape when needed.
ideas.name: Folding Terminal

verdict.money_why: Ordinary people buy it, and the firms that already make and sell pocket computers add the feature and collect.
verdict.prize_why: Folding or bending is a convenience added to a pocket computer people would own anyway.

ideas.author: Ray Naylor
ideas.line: An ultrathin electronic sheet that displays content like a printed page.
ideas.name: Palimpscreen

verdict.money_why: Ordinary people buy it, and the firms that already make and sell screens and pocket computers add the feature and collect.
verdict.prize_why: A screen as thin and light as paper is a general display that could replace print and fixed sets, which changes the costs of a whole industry.

ideas.author: M.T. Hill
ideas.line: A cheap network connection device meant to be discarded after use.
ideas.name: Burner Modem

verdict.money_why: People buy it for themselves and it is cheap by design and simple to make, so no seller keeps much.
verdict.prize_why: A network connection you throw away after use serves the few who want not to be traced.

ideas.author: Bruce Sterling
ideas.line: Robots able to handle all upkeep and repair work aboard a ship.
ideas.name: Maritime Robots

verdict.money_why: Ship and plant operators buy them, and as the machines can be copied the established makers that already equip and service those operators collect.
verdict.prize_why: Robots that do all upkeep and repair aboard a ship would cut crew costs across shipping.

ideas.author: Bruce Sterling
ideas.line: Powered gloves that boost a sailor's grip and handling of lines.
ideas.name: Prosthetic Yachting Gloves

verdict.money_why: Sailors buy them for themselves, and many makers could build such gloves.
verdict.prize_why: Gloves that strengthen a sailor's grip are a convenience for a pastime.

ideas.author: M.T. Hill
ideas.line: A drug that puts a traveller into a brief hibernation-like torpor for the length of a flight.
ideas.name: Sloth Pill
ideas.profit: a fat profit, kept by the maker

verdict.money_why: Travellers would buy it for themselves, and a new drug is protected from copying for a while, so its maker keeps what is left.
verdict.prize_why: Sleeping through a single flight is a comfort for travellers, unlike the long dormancy that makes far voyages possible.

ideas.author: Nick Harkaway
ideas.line: A moldable tissue substitute pressed into wounds to fill damaged flesh.
ideas.name: Flesh Putty
ideas.profit: a fat profit, kept by incumbent firms

verdict.money_why: Hospitals and clinics would buy it, and the firms that already supply wound dressings could all make it, so they collect a modest margin.
verdict.prize_why: Man-made skin helps people with burns and bad wounds, which is an important but narrow part of medicine.

ideas.author: David Gerrold
ideas.line: A brain implant that supports an autistic child in daily functioning and learning.
ideas.name: Bio-Implant (Compensator Chip)
ideas.profit: a fat profit, kept by the maker

verdict.money_why: Families or their insurers would pay, and the makers of medical implants who already hold hospital trust could copy it and collect.
verdict.prize_why: Helping autistic children manage daily life and learning would be worth a great deal to many families.

ideas.author: Ray Naylor
ideas.line: A crewless cargo ship that sails itself while hauling goods for trade.
ideas.name: Autofreighter

verdict.money_why: Freight carriers buy it, and since the self-steering gear can be copied, the carriers and builders that already own the fleets and routes collect.
verdict.prize_why: Hauling goods with no crew aboard changes the costs of a whole freight industry.

ideas.author: M.T. Hill
ideas.line: A fictional mouth insert used by characters to defeat genetic identity tests.
ideas.name: DNA Swab Palate

verdict.money_why: Assuming a spy service is the lawful buyer, it pays, and since others could copy the insert the firms already trusted with secret supply work collect.
verdict.prize_why: An insert that defeats identity tests serves only the few agents who must pass as someone else, and is forbidden to everyone else.

ideas.author: M.T. Hill
ideas.line: Flying monitoring robots that play soothing sounds to settle people below.
ideas.name: Pacification Drones

verdict.money_why: Police forces pay, and gear sold to them goes through the firms that already hold their supply contracts.
verdict.prize_why: Flying robots that watch crowds and calm them would change how a state keeps order in public places.

ideas.author: David Gerrold
ideas.line: A general-purpose watching robot that moves by clambering over surfaces instead of flying.
ideas.name: Scuttle-bot

verdict.money_why: Assumes it watches people for a state; once made it can be copied, so the firms already supplying such services collect.
verdict.prize_why: A crawling robot that watches where flying ones cannot changes what police and spy services can learn.

ideas.author: Ray Naylor
ideas.line: A face covering that conceals who the wearer is from observers and cameras.
ideas.name: Abglanz

verdict.money_why: Ordinary people buy it, and a face covering is easy for any maker to copy so no seller keeps much.
verdict.prize_why: Hiding your face from cameras is wanted by a minority who care strongly about privacy.

ideas.author: Neal Stephenson
ideas.line: A giant gun firing reflective particles into the upper sky to cool the planet.
ideas.name: Pina2bo
ideas.profit: not judged (not a technology, not something sold, not physically possible, or unclear)

verdict.money_why: Nobody can be charged one by one, so a government pays, and the gun and the particles are plain engineering that many builders could supply.
verdict.prize_why: Cooling the whole planet would touch the weather and harvests of nearly everyone, for good or ill.

ideas.author: Nick Harkaway
ideas.line: Furniture cultivated from the owner's own genetic material to fit them comfortably.
ideas.name: Science Chair

verdict.money_why: People buy it for the home, and since living stock multiplies once any of it is sold, no originator can hold it, so the breeders and furnishing shops that already hold stock and showrooms collect.
verdict.prize_why: A chair grown to fit its owner is a novel way to get comfortable furniture.
